issues.passage: He refused to vacate the apartment and signed a three-year extension instead.
issues.why: Refusing to vacate is natural, correct use of vacate = leave a place; the extension explains staying, not a misuse of the verb.

fix.correctPassage: Tenants were ordered to vacate the building within thirty days.
wrongPassages: The firm will vacate the office by moving additional staff into the same suite.
He plans to vacate the apartment by renewing the lease and remaining for three more years.
Organizers plan to vacate the hall by packing every available seat before the doors open.

issues.passage: She refused to extrapolate, reporting only results that fell inside the measured range.
issues.why: Refusing to extrapolate and staying within measured data is correct use of extrapolate = extend conclusions beyond known data.

fix.correctPassage: It is risky to extrapolate from such a small sample to the whole population.
wrongPassages: She tried to extrapolate by reporting only results that fell inside the measured range.
They chose to extrapolate the dataset by discarding every observation past the first year.
He tried to extrapolate the trend by averaging only the known points and stopping there.
